lawyer:
Abdul Momin Talukder, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Farid Ahmed Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the Opposite Party
parties:
Subash Chandra Chowdhury and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment: 5. From the order impugned I find that on 31.12.1984 the learned Judge returned the memorandum to the filing advocate for presentation of the same for the second time with a fresh application for condonation of delay explaining each day's delay in filing the appeal and on return the appeal was filed on 8.5.1985. It appears from the judgment that Mr. Azizur Rahman, the learned Asstt. Government Pleader was in-charge of the suit and he did not report the result of the suit to the appellant. From the judgment I find that the suit was decreed on 5.3.1984 and result was noted by Mr. Azizur Rahman. It also appears that the plaintiff on 5.5.1984 applied to the ADC (Rev), Pabna for correction of the records of right on the basis of the judgment and decree passed in the OC. Suit No. 3 of 1978 and on 7.5.1985 the ADC (Rev), Pabna forwarded the application to the Govt, Pleader for opinion. Thus, it appears that the Government through its Officer, the ADC (Rev), Pabna and the learned Government Pleader had the knowledge of the decree much earlier than 13.10.1984 which is said to be the date of knowledge of the appellant about the result of the suit. Thus, on facts of this case I also find that the learned Judge committed illegality as the impugned order is the result of his non-application of judicial mind in condoning the delay and in registering the appeal. The right accrued to the petitioner by lapse of time is a vested right and the learned District Judge should not have dealt with the matter so lightly as he has done in the instant case. In exercise of his discretion he must have exercised the same with due caution and not whimsically. I am of the opinion that the order impugned calls for interference.
